 Football
 Soccer-MLS announces key 2027 'Sprint Season' matches ahead of calendar shift
 Thursday, 29 Oct 2026
 | 8:13 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Oct 10, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Inter Miami CF forward Leo Messi (10) dribbles the ball against D.C. United during the second half at Nu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images/File Photo 
 Oct 28 (Reuters) - Lionel Messi's ⁠Inter Miami will kick off Major League Soccer's 2027 "Sprint Season" when ⁠they face Cincinnati on February 19, launching the league's transition ‌to a traditional autumn-to-spring calendar.
 The standalone match at Nu Stadium in Miami will begin a truncated 14-game regular season and playoff tournament designed to bridge the gap ​as MLS shifts away from its traditional ⁠summer schedule to align with ⁠Europe's top leagues.
 The schedule, previewed on Apple TV's "MLS Countdown," emphasizes weekly rivalry ⁠matchups. ‌Among the headline games announced, LA Galaxy will host Los Angeles FC on April 10 in the "El Trafico" derby.
 The ⁠sprint season will conclude its regular-season slate on ​May 8 with "Decision Day," ‌anchored by the Hudson River Derby between New York City ⁠FC and ​the New York Red Bulls, setting the stage for the May playoffs.
 The four-month sprint serves as the prelude to the league's full operational shift. ⁠The first standard season under the new timetable ​will run from mid-to-late July 2027 through May 2028, featuring a midwinter break and no matches in January.
 MLS Commissioner Don Garber previously called ⁠the calendar change "one of the most important decisions in our history."
 The strategic overhaul was approved following a two-year review to synchronize the league's transfer activity with the global summer window, minimize scheduling conflicts with ​FIFA's international fixtures, and hold the MLS Cup ⁠playoffs in May when the North American sports calendar is less crowded.
 US ​men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino is ‌among those who have endorsed the ​change, noting that calendar alignment with the global soccer landscape will benefit clubs, coaches, and player development.
 (Reporting by Rory Carroll)
